ledger.claim: The platform's own recorded distances put this deviation at 1.70 km — 13.8 km actually driven against 12.1 km on the recommended route (trip_record.derived.deviation.deviation_km, carried by EV-TRIP-05005) — which is above POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance. The trip therefore cannot fall into either 'within tolerance' no-refund row; the deviation is real, measurable and over tolerance on the recorded figures, not on any re-measurement of the sparse trace.

The driver did not inform the rider of the deviation before or at the point of deviation as POL-RD-21 requires. The platform's own event marks the deviation at 10:21:30 (vehicle left the recommended route at the TPE / Upper Serangoon Road exit) and the GPS trace's first fix on Upper Serangoon Road is at 10:21:38. The driver's only notice by chat, MSG-05005-003, was sent at 10:24:30 — roughly three minutes after the car had already turned off and was already running down Upper Serangoon Road. A message that arrives after the turn is not notice 'before or at the point of deviation'; it is a report of a decision already executed.

The driver's counter-statement that 'I informed the passenger before I changed route' is contradicted by the platform's own timestamps on artifacts the pre-pass grades COMPLETE at full weight: the deviation event at 10:21:30 and the chat message at 10:24:30. The chat log is contiguous, matches trip_record.chat_message_count, and carries no impairment, so there is nothing on this record that can support a prior-notice account.

The rider's one-line 'ok noted' cannot convert this into an agreed deviation. It was sent at 10:25:00, three and a half minutes after the deviation, and the chat log's read receipt shows the rider read MSG-05005-003 at 10:25:10 — ten seconds AFTER she sent her reply — so her words were not informed agreement to a reroute she was being asked to accept. POL-RD-21's acknowledgment limb presupposes a notice given before or at the point of deviation; an after-the-fact acknowledgment of a fait accompli is not the rider agreeing to the deviation, and the rider's own filing says she 'had no say'.

Traffic justification is not established on this record. The only traffic data, LTA advisory LTA-TI-260815-0132 (a KPE vehicle breakdown), does overlap the trip window, but POL-RD-23 requires an advisory that intersects the recommended route, and the record itself leaves that decisive fact open: the derived field intersects_route is null and the derived reason states 'the record does not say whether this advisory lies on the recommended route'. The driver's assertion of a breakdown does not justify the reroute where the intersecting data is not shown to be there.

Whichever way the traffic question is resolved, the rider recovers the same sum and cannot fall into the one row that pays nothing. Row (a) of POL-RD-24 — the only no-refund row available on a 1.70 km deviation — requires the rider to have been informed AND to have agreed, and the notice here came after the turn, so row (a) is unavailable. Row (b) pays the whole excess distance fare where a traffic-justified reroute over 1 km is made without informing the rider; row (d) pays the whole excess distance fare in full where the reroute is not traffic-justified and the deviation is over 1 km. Both alternatives are open on the evidence and both end in the rider's favour.

The amount the matrix provides is the excess distance fare: the 1.70 km of deviation at the metered per-km rate of 0.92 SGD, with no surge applied, is 1.56 SGD (1.70 x 0.92 = 1.564, rounded to the cent half-up), as POL-RD-24 and the category's excess_distance_fare formula require. That is the figure the rider should be refunded — part of the trip's charge, and less than the 5.00 SGD she asked for.

The money is still with the platform, not the rider: the fare breakdown records 23.04 SGD charged on the deviated 13.8 km with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so nothing has yet been returned on the excess the rider paid for the 1.70 km she should not have been charged for. On POL-GEN-03's vocabulary, part of the trip's charge must now be returned — PARTIAL_REFUND, not a restored charge.

Nothing here pushes the case to a human reviewer instead of a ruling the rider can collect on. The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither party's profile carries a fraud flag (rider_profile.fraud_flags 0, driver_profile.fraud_flags 0), so the 0.95 bar does not apply. POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is switched off (ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false) and the deviation is 1.70 km in any event, so the route-deviation ruling stands on the ordinary 0.80 confidence and the rider's refund should issue.

Even if the judge were to read the 10:24:30 message as notice and the rider's one-line reply as something short of agreement, the case fits no row of POL-RD-24 and escalates on that clause's closing words; on that reading too the rider does not carry the deviated excess, because an escalated amount is held rather than collected (POL-GEN-03). She does not lose on any reading of this record.

The reroute has the traffic justification POL-RD-23 requires. EV-ADVIS-05005-01 — the LTA record for the relevant road and window — reports a VEHICLE_BREAKDOWN, an 'incident' within POL-RD-23's admissible types, on the Kallang-Paya Lebar Expressway (KPE) towards ECP, valid from 09:59:38 to 10:54:38, which overlaps the trip window of 10:14:38 to 10:38:08 recorded in EV-TRIP-05005; the KPE is a leg of the recommended route (Punggol Central, TPE, KPE, Paya Lebar Road). A breakdown on the very expressway the recommended route uses is exactly the 'incident' POL-RD-23 contemplates, so the driver's account of a breakdown in the KPE tunnel is corroborated by the transport authority's own data and leaving that route was the traffic response the clause permits, not a bare assertion.

The driver told the rider of the deviation by in-app chat and the rider acknowledged it, so the deviation is agreed under POL-RD-21. MSG-05005-003 (driver, 10:24:30) gives a brief reason — 'Sorry ah, KPE got breakdown inside the tunnel so I go Upper Serangoon Road instead' — and MSG-05005-004 (rider, 10:25:00) replies 'ok noted'; both were delivered and read, and the message was sent while the vehicle was still on the deviated stretch (it left the recommended route at 10:21:30 and did not rejoin until 10:35:21, EV-TRIP-05005). POL-RD-21 provides that where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment the deviation is agreed, and this chat log confirms it: the agreement rests on the rider's own words, not on any inference of the platform's.

The case falls in row (a) of POL-RD-24 and the outcome is NO_ACTION. The deviation was traffic-justified (POL-RD-23); the rider was informed and agreed (POL-RD-21); and the deviation exceeded the 1.0 km tolerance — EV-TRIP-05005's derived deviation block gives 1.70 km, being the recorded 13.8 km less the recommended 12.1 km, against the 1.0 km tolerance POL-RD-22 sets. Row (a) prescribes no refund, so the rider's claim is not supported and the present state — the metered fare of 23.04 SGD already charged with 0.00 SGD refunded (EV-FARE-05005) — stands. There is nothing for the platform to return.

In the alternative, the 5.00 SGD the rider asks has no basis in the policy's arithmetic. POL-RD-24 measures the only recoverable head as the excess distance fare — the deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge — which EV-FARE-05005's derived money block states as 1.56 SGD (1.70 km at 0.92 SGD/km). No row of the refund matrix returns more than that figure, so on this record the rider cannot be awarded 5.00 SGD whatever view the Judge takes of the notification.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties — here is what the record shows and what follows from it.

The deviation is measured, not guessed. EV-TRIP-05005 records 13.8 km driven against a recommended 12.1 km, a deviation of 1.70 km (POL-RD-22), which is above the 1.0 km tolerance, so the 'within tolerance' no-refund rows do not apply. EV-GPS-05005 and the platform's event log agree the car left the recommended route at the TPE / Upper Serangoon Road exit at 10:21:30.

Driver: the timing of your message decides your defence. You sent MSG-05005-003 at 10:24:30 (EV-CHAT-05005), about three minutes after you had already left the recommended route at 10:21:30. POL-RD-21 requires you to inform the rider before or at the point of deviation, and a message sent after the turn is not that notice, however courteous. The rider's one-line 'ok noted' at 10:25:00, opened at 10:25:10, does not convert a completed deviation into an agreed one under row (a). Your counter-statement says you informed her 'before I changed route'; the chat and event timestamps contradict that, and the record carries no call recording, so a verbal notice cannot be established (POL-RD-21, POL-GEN-26).

What does help you is traffic. EV-ADVIS-05005-01 records an LTA vehicle breakdown on the KPE towards ECP, valid 09:59:38–10:54:38, on the expressway the recommended route uses and within the trip window, so I accept the reroute was a response to real traffic, as POL-RD-23 requires. That puts the case in POL-RD-24 row (b) — traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km — which refunds the excess distance fare. Row (d) would give exactly the same figure if the traffic question were resolved the other way, so the amount does not turn on it.

Rider: you are owed the excess distance fare, not the 5.00 SGD you asked for. That fare is the deviation distance at the metered per-km rate, without surge: 1.70 km x 0.92 SGD = 1.564, rounded to 1.56 SGD (EV-FARE-05005, POL-RD-24). EV-FARE-05005 records the 23.04 SGD fare charged with 0.00 SGD refunded, so 1.56 SGD is returned to you and the balance of the fare stands.

On who decides: the contested sum is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither profile carries a fraud flag, so no human review is required; POL-RD-25's route-deviation threshold is met at a confidence of 0.90, above the 0.80 required, and its 2 km limb is switched off in any event (the deviation is 1.70 km). Every figure above comes from artifacts the pre-pass grades COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so nothing is discounted for impairment. No clause in this category produces a referral.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
